data.description:
Addendum to the Texas component of existing finding #67: expands its single linked report into a seven-report May 17 sequence, verifies the sign-in/401 outcomes and distinguishes unverified converter bodies and passive links from actual data recovery. This does not alter its Wisconsin or Connecticut components.

Seven linked URLQuery reports on May 17, 2026, 08:36:24-11:01:25 UTC concern the Texas DSHS Tableau STD dashboard/export route: two direct PDF attempts, three converter-route reports (including two TinyURL submissions), and two passive link wrappers. The two newly identified shortener reports extend the earlier five-report cluster but add neither a new workbook nor another day of activity.

Only the two direct PDF reports record DSHS-host traffic. Each export navigates to sign-in, and its session check returns 401. Other POSTs are unauthenticated login-interface operations; a ListIdentityPools 201 is not proof of account creation. Across those two reports, 216 DSHS HTTP entries largely represent the sign-in page and assets, not 216 dataset reads. There is no recorded credential submission or authenticated export.

The three converter records share metadata for a 5,943-byte text/markdown response and the same response hash. The original bodies could not be recovered, so HTTP 200 and matching fingerprints establish consistent responses, not successful CSV or disease-data extraction. Proxy-side contacts may be invisible in browser records. The two HTTPBin wrappers contain links only; an older annotation treating one as a static data result was incorrect.

One direct submission contains Gonorrhea/2021 strings, with encoded separators whose parsing is unverified. A separate passive link includes Potter as an area. Those selectors must not be combined into a demonstrated Potter/Gonorrhea/2021 query. The target is an aggregate STD dashboard; the records do not establish individual patient access, authentication bypass or exploit-shaped escalation. The None cyberattack tag reflects that narrower evidence.

The records support persistence across alternative retrieval routes while stopping at an observed sign-in boundary, with converter outcomes unresolved. No common operator, AI author/provider or authorization context is established. Untapped source is No for this seven-report cluster: expanded searches and the retained reports have been reviewed; inaccessible converter bytes and archive coverage gaps are limitations rather than a claimed new substantial corpus.
data.summary: Seven May 17 URLQuery reports show repeated Texas DSHS aggregate-data export attempts through direct, converter and shortener routes. Direct PDFs hit sign-in/401; converter success and data extraction remain unverified.
